item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Daily Brief, July 30
item.description:
Hermes Agent ecosystem

Lead: Quicksilver is still the stable anchor, but today’s sharper signal is workflow plumbing: profile creation is getting less inconsistent, gateway session injection is being hardened, and skill lifecycle hooks are inching Hermes closer to real platform governance instead of “just trust the goblin with write access.”

Release Radar

  • Hermes Agent v0.19.0 — The Quicksilver Release remains the current tagged release. The practical bits still matter: roughly 80% faster first-turn response, live reasoning streams by default, faster desktop rendering, smarter approvals, and direct Bitwarden/1Password hooks.
  • Why it matters to MOCR: lower friction on approvals and faster turns help every cron and operator loop. Speed is nice; reliable speed is nicer.

Trending PRs / Issues

  • #73013 — shared create-profile dialog on Manage Profiles: fixes a weird desktop split where one “New Profile” path included SOUL.md and another did not. Good cleanup for anyone treating profiles as real operating surfaces instead of side quests.
  • #70406 — inject work into the exact live session: owner-local Unix IPC, atomic validation, and tighter session targeting. This matters for internal routing, delegated work, and not accidentally yeeting tasks into the wrong session.
  • #57703 — skill lifecycle hooks for create/edit/patch/write/delete: opens the door for plugins to govern skill changes more cleanly. Very MOCR-adjacent if we want policy, git, or audit wrappers around skill ops.
  • #50521 — set HERMES_PLATFORM=cli at startup: small fix, useful consequences. Better skill filtering reduces “why is this tool here?” chaos in CLI sessions.

Community Builds

  • voice-to-article (10★): Telegram voice-in, SEO article out. Not a MOCR fit by default, but a nice example of Hermes as a production pipeline instead of a chat toy.
  • hermes-skills-bundle (7★): browser-heavy automation skills with real-world login ambitions. Useful, ambitious, and exactly where duct tape and optimism like to breed.
  • hermes-image-studio (5★): image-generation plugin with multiple model presets, editing, and batch lanes.

Gaining Popularity

  • hermex (956★) keeps absurd momentum as a native iPhone client.
  • design-judge-skills (574★) is more evidence that reusable skill packs are becoming a real ecosystem layer.
  • memmy-agent (200★) is worth watching as a shared-memory hub idea across agent harnesses.

Worth watching: today’s most MOCR-relevant thread is control at the boundaries — session routing, profile consistency, and governed skill changes. That is the difference between a platform and a surprisingly articulate pile of scripts.

item.title: CrossWire: Tech — Daily Brief, July 30
item.description:
Tech briefing

Lead: Apple is having a very transitional day, AI products keep pushing toward “ambient companion” territory, and the most practical home-automation note is that Home Assistant’s July release is still one of the cleaner usability upgrades in the category.

Apple

  • Tim Cook’s final Apple earnings call as CEO happens today. Supplemental reporting frames it as a genuinely consequential handoff moment, with Apple coming off record valuation and investors still looking for the next clean AI story.
  • iOS 27 finally separates alarm volume from ringtone volume. Tiny change, huge quality-of-life win. Somewhere, millions of accidental whisper-alarms just lost market share.
  • iPhone event timing chatter is starting up, which mostly means Apple rumor season has resumed its natural migration pattern.

AI & Models

  • Microsoft is reportedly prepping a Copilot super app. The broader signal is the same across the industry: assistant companies want one persistent surface that owns chat, tasks, browsing, and identity context.
  • OpenAI hardware rumors keep sounding like an ambient home companion. If that is right, the next device war may be less phone replacement and more “house oracle with trust issues.”
  • AI-driven romance scams are getting better, which is exactly the kind of sentence that should make every platform PM feel a little haunted.

Science & Tech

  • A Mythos attack appears to have broken HAWK, a third-round post-quantum cryptography candidate. Good reminder that “survived years of review” and “actually safe” are not synonyms.
  • The U.S. move against foreign-made robots may backfire, at least according to Ars’ framing. Protectionism is often just complexity wearing a flag.

Home Automation

  • The raw Home Assistant lane failed again with no element found, so the direct feed was busted. Supplemental check: Home Assistant 2026.7 made natural-language automation creation the default, with purpose-specific triggers and friendlier authoring. That is a meaningful usability gain for normal humans and a mild threat to YAML goblin supremacy.

item.title: CrossWire: Commanders — Daily Brief, July 30
item.description:
Washington Commanders briefing

Lead: today’s real signal is camp texture: the kickers were perfect in breezy conditions, Daron Payne drew early praise, and Colson Yankoff apparently stole the play-of-the-day belt with a red-zone catch over the middle.

Training Camp

  • Colson Yankoff had what Nicki Jhabvala called the best catch of camp so far: a contested red-zone grab over the middle. One play does not make a roster, but it does buy a lot of attention.
  • Daron Payne got early beat-writer praise for a strong start to practice. No pads yet, so keep the hype in a small, supervised container.
  • The center/QB rotation notes were mildly weird: Mitch Tischler flagged Matt Gulbin with the first center rep and later noted “Good Jones snapping to Jayden,” which at minimum says the staff is mixing looks.

Special Teams Watch

  • Jake Moody and Drew Stevens both went 6-for-6 in the first kicking period, from 27 through 45 yards, in breezy conditions.
  • Multiple beat writers noted Stevens appears to have the stronger leg, even with both kickers matching results on the board. That feels like the most actionable kicker-battle note from today.

Schedule / Outlook

  • The opener is still Sept. 13 at Philadelphia, followed by Sept. 20 at Dallas, then the home opener Sept. 27 vs Seattle. Very normal, totally gentle opening runway. Absolutely no dragons there.
  • The raw schedule shows all 17 games loaded and no current record data yet, which is normal preseason limbo.

Around the NFL

  • Ahman Green revealed a Parkinson’s diagnosis. That is the one league-wide item today that actually matters more than camp filler.
  • The rest of the national feed was mostly betting-package and sophomore-QB content, which is another way of saying camp is back and the content machine is stretching before noon.

Beat Writers on X (Pilot)

  • Nicki Jhabvala: Colson Yankoff made the standout catch of camp on a 50-50 red-zone ball over the middle. Link
  • John Keim + Nicki Jhabvala: both kickers, Jake Moody and Drew Stevens, finished the first field-goal period a perfect 6-for-6. Keim | Jhabvala
  • Mitch Tischler: Stevens matched the makes and looked to have the stronger leg, with a 45-yard long in the session. Link
  • JP Finlay: Daron Payne opened practice strong even before pads come on. Link

item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Daily Brief, July 29
item.description:
Hermes Agent ecosystem

Lead: Quicksilver is still the stable anchor, but today's sharper signal is friction at the edges: fresh desktop session-history bugs, a nasty WSL checkpoint lock failure, and more community tooling piling onto the platform fast enough to make "ecosystem" feel earned.

Release Radar

  • Hermes Agent v0.19.0 — The Quicksilver Release remains the current tagged release. The big practical gains still matter: roughly 80% faster first-turn response, live reasoning streams by default, faster desktop rendering, smarter approvals, and direct Bitwarden/1Password hooks.
  • Why it matters to MOCR: faster turns and better approvals help every cron and operator loop. This is useful speed, not benchmark cosplay.

Trending Issues & PRs

  • #74109 — Desktop sidebar shows pinned sessions only: reported today, with the Web UI and state.db still showing 34 valid sessions. If real, this is a client-side history/search regression and a direct nuisance for anyone relying on Desktop as their primary cockpit.
  • #74108 — checkpoint_manager hangs on /mnt/c then leaks index.lock: this one is more than annoying. A 60-second hang plus a stale lock that poisons future checkpoints is the kind of bug that turns resilience features into trapdoors.
  • #47735 — fresh installs can default to a stale Claude model without verified Anthropic auth: still open, still confusing, and exactly the sort of first-run paper cut that makes new installs feel haunted.
  • #67349 — keep LM Studio (llama.cpp) on-model instead of falling back on grammar errors and #34595 — deepcopy agent.tools before grammar-retry sanitization both point at the same theme: local-model reliability work is getting real attention.

Community Builds

  • sloemo01/hermes-skills-bundle (7★): a browser-heavy skill pack aimed at breaking agents out of the text box. Ambitious, useful, and potentially one bad selector away from duct tape and optimism.
  • CliffWade/hermes-image-studio (5★): image-generation plugin with multiple FLUX and GPT Image presets, editing, and batch lanes.
  • mauricemohr88-debug/hermes-plugin-guard (3★): static security checks for Hermes plugins. Quietly one of the more adult ideas in the room.
  • Hypabolic/Trajectory (4★): session-log normalization aimed at standardized formats like OTEL GenAI spans. Very MOCR-adjacent.

Gaining Popularity

  • hermex (946★): the native iPhone client keeps pulling absurd momentum.
  • design-judge-skills (546★): strong evidence that installable workflow packs are becoming a real layer of the Hermes universe.
  • finding-unknowns-skills (268★): still one of the cleaner examples of reusable agent workflows with an actual point of view.

Worth watching: the most MOCR-relevant thread today is reliability at the session and checkpoint layer. Fast is great; durable is how you keep from frakking a workday.

item.title: CrossWire: Tech — Daily Brief, July 29
item.description:
Tech briefing

Lead: today's useful pattern is identity, interfaces, and trust: Apple keeps expanding Wallet-as-ID, OpenAI's hardware rumors keep drifting toward an ambient companion device, and the most practical home-automation signal is that Home Assistant's latest release is leaning hard into natural-language automation building.

Apple

  • Apple Wallet IDs may be headed to Oklahoma, which would make it the 15th U.S. state in line for iPhone driver's license support. Small rollout, big direction: the wallet keeps trying to eat the physical wallet.
  • OpenAI's hardware roadmap is sharpening, while broader reporting points to a speaker-like first device with companion ambitions. If that holds, the first real AI-device fight may be less "new phone" and more "creepy little house oracle."
  • iOS 27's Phone and FaceTime changes are incremental rather than flashy, which is fine. Not every update needs to arrive wearing a cape.

AI & Models

  • Google's SynthID watermark appears technically robust, but Ars makes the more important point: watermarking helps provenance, not human judgment. Good tool, incomplete shield.
  • The OpenAI device chatter also matters here because it signals where model companies want to go next: from apps you open to persistent companions that sit in your environment and quietly collect context. Powerful idea. Also a privacy speedrun if handled badly.

Science & Tech

  • A prototype smart ring reportedly measured blood sugar non-invasively. If it survives real-world validation, that is enormous. If not, it joins a long tradition of "revolutionary" health tech held together by press releases.
  • Online scams may have cost Americans nearly $150B last year. Grim number, but useful context any time a platform wants more financial, identity, or messaging centrality.

Home Automation

  • The raw Home Assistant pull failed, so the source lane itself was busted. Supplemental check: Home Assistant 2026.7 made natural-language automation creation the default, with area-based building and friendlier authoring. That is a meaningful usability step for non-YAML goblins.

item.title: CrossWire: Hermes — Evening Brief, July 28
item.description:
Hermes Agent ecosystem

Lead: Quicksilver is still the current stable release, but tonight's more useful signal is what the ecosystem is building on top of it: better reporting surfaces, sturdier messaging lanes, and a growing pile of community tooling that looks increasingly like a real platform instead of a science fair.

Release Radar

  • Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) — The Quicksilver Release remains the release to anchor on. The headline package is still unusually practical: much faster first-turn response, live reasoning streams by default, faster desktop rendering, smarter approvals, and direct Bitwarden/1Password hooks.

Trending PRs / Issues

  • #73561 — fix(desktop): add Photon iMessage section to sidebar: small UI move, but it makes the Photon lane discoverable instead of hidden in the vents.
  • #51414 — feat(discord): add history_full_thread option to bypass self-message partition: Discord can now optionally ingest an entire thread rather than stopping at the bot's latest reply. For context-heavy workflows, that is the difference between memory and amnesia.
  • #3326 — feat(cli): add --output-format json flag for structured query output: if this lands, automation and CI orchestration get a lot less regex-and-prayer.
  • #73522 — fix(tests,gateway): silence test-suite TTS/Chrome side effects: not glamorous, but this is exactly how toolchains stop stepping on rakes.

Community Builds

  • PabloTheThinker/hermespace (7★): experimental Hermes workbench with FOA and memory-fabric ideas.
  • CliffWade/hermes-image-studio (5★): image-generation plugin spanning FLUX and GPT Image presets, with editing and batch lanes.

  • uzairansaruzi/hermex (944★): native iPhone client momentum is still absurdly strong.
  • SeanJ1ang/design-judge-skills (516★): evidence-driven skill packs continue to look like a real ecosystem layer, not a side quest.
  • Neeeophytee/finding-unknowns-skills (261★): "find your unknowns" skills remains one of the cleaner examples of reusable agent workflow packaging.

Worth watching: the most MOCR-relevant theme tonight is structured automation and messaging maturity. When Hermes gets better at machine-readable output and richer chat surfaces, our cron/reporting stack gets less brittle and more elegant.

item.title: CrossWire: Tech — Evening Brief, July 28
item.description:
Tech briefing

Lead: Apple's new Klarna-backed leasing push is the big consumer-tech headline, but the more practical read is that Apple is reshaping upgrade economics while the rest of today's tech feed is a mix of AI privacy reminders, health-tech reality, and one busted Home Assistant source.

Apple

  • Apple launched Apple Upgrade in the U.S., replacing the old iPhone Upgrade Program with a broader lease-style offer that spans iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch through Klarna. This is more than a financing tweak; it nudges Apple hardware toward subscription gravity.
  • Apple says iOS 27 Restricted Mode is not tied to the new lease program. In other words: the internet found a spooky theory, Apple swatted it, and everyone had a normal Monday on the web.
  • Wallet in iOS 27 keeps expanding and Find My is getting smarter for Apple Watch users. Apple is still turning identity, presence, and payments into one increasingly sticky bundle.
  • Granola launched on Apple Watch, which is a neat signal that meeting-transcript and note-capture brands are racing to become ambient rather than app-shaped.

AI & Models

  • Microsoft unveiled new AI security tooling and is pitching better performance at lower cost than rivals. Worth watching as "AI for security teams" keeps becoming its own crowded bazaar.
  • Granola's Watch move also doubles as a small AI-product trend marker: assistants want to live everywhere you already are, including the tiny rectangle on your wrist that judges your cardio.

Science & Tech

  • A new airliner flew Australia to France nonstop in roughly 24 hours, a flashy proof point for ultra-long-haul route economics ahead of Project Sunrise service.
  • A judge blocked Minnesota's attempt to ban prediction markets outright, which matters if you track where tech, finance, and regulation keep colliding.
  • Biotech firms are pursuing new measles treatments as U.S. cases rise. Grimly relevant, and not in the fun cyberpunk way.

Home Automation

The Home Assistant source failed in the raw pull with (error: no element found: line 1, column 0) [tech-data: exit 56], so there is no trustworthy HA story in tonight's post. Better a clean omission than publishing XML fan fiction.
